items.title: Inventory cloud storage, identities, endpoints, and data classes
items.objective: Map buckets/containers, accounts/projects/subscriptions, regions, CDN/origins, workloads, owners, and intended public/private data before active tests.
prerequisites: Confirmed cloud/storage provider, account/project/subscription, and owner-approved scope
Synthetic uniquely prefixed objects, designated identities, and policy/log evidence as applicable
steps: Map provider/account/container/origin/identity/data-class and intended access contract
Create or identify a uniquely prefixed synthetic control object/policy fixture
Change one principal, object key, capability, policy condition, origin, lifecycle, event, or delivery context
Verify effective provider decision and audit evidence, then remove all test objects/capabilities/state

examples.note: Use only uniquely prefixed synthetic objects and designated test identities; fully redact URLs, keys, credentials, and account IDs.

items.manipulate: One cloud principal, container/object key, signed capability, policy condition, origin, lifecycle, event, or browser context at a time
items.secure_behavior: Storage access is private by default, explicitly authorized by principal/action/resource/tenant, least-privileged, short-lived where delegated, isolated from metadata/egress abuse, lifecycle-controlled, and audited.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a live material store or trust relationship remains unowned, unclassified, or outside assessment coverage
items.validation: Confirm effective provider access or policy behavior with a synthetic object and distinguish public design, signed capability semantics, conditional denies, caching, and asynchronous lifecycle/event behavior.
false_positives: provider-managed service buckets can be dependency-only
one logical product can intentionally span multiple accounts/regions
items.impact: A confirmed cloud/storage weakness can expose or alter tenant data, leak workload credentials, bypass edge controls, grant persistent cross-account access, destroy/retain protected objects, or trigger privileged downstream systems.
evidence: Provider/account/container/object aliases with sensitive IDs redacted
Anonymous and designated-principal request/policy decision
Signed capability, origin, lifecycle, event, or IAM conditions
Synthetic before/after object state, audit event, cleanup, and credential revocation
tools: Provider CLI with designated test identity
Burp Repeater for public/signed endpoints
Provider policy simulator and audit logs
items.remediation: Use private-by-default storage, explicit least-privilege identity/resource/tenant policies, narrow expiring capabilities, isolated origins/metadata/egress, safe lifecycle/event consumers, encryption where required, and complete audit logging.
